transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (NebulaPay CTO), Mark Rivera (Head of ML infra), Priya Patel (Security)

Summary (auto): go-through on latency/throughput targets, clarify concurrency and streaming needs, next steps to run benchmarks and share security docs.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Sofia): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood, this is Liam our SE. Could we do quick intros?
00:08 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Hi, I'm Aisha, CTO at NebulaPay. We run a payments assistant that helps users with refunds, disputes, and quick reconciliations. We're looking at adding an LLM chat layer.
00:18 Speaker 3 (Mark): Mark here, I run ML infra, I'm responsible for latency and capacity planning.
00:22 Speaker 4 (Priya): Priya, security and compliance. We'll need SOC2 and KMS integration details.
00:28 Speaker 1 (Sofia): Great, thank you. Main goal for today is to understand your p95 latency requirements, concurrency, streaming needs, and whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private makes sense.
00:40 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Correct. Our success metric is p95 end-to-end under production load. We aim for p95 of around 300ms for short, 32-token answers in the chat UI. If that's unrealistic we can relax but that's the target.
00:55 Speaker 3 (Mark): For concurrency, typical peak concurrent chats per shard is ~50, but during promos we can spike to 200 concurrent sessions. Average message length is 20-80 tokens, streaming is important so we can show tokens as they generate to improve UX.
01:12 Speaker 1 (Sofia): Thanks that's super helpful. Liam, quick thought?
01:15 Speaker 5 (Liam): Yeah, two immediate signals — p95 300ms for a 32-token response at concurrency 50 is a tight SLO when using larger models. For optimized open models on good GPU instance types (A100/H100 class), we can typically hit 250-500ms p95 for small-ish seq lengths with Dedicated. Hosted can also get there but depends on tenancy and noisy neighbors.
01:38 Speaker 3 (Mark): Can you define what you mean by "p95" — is that server-only generation time, or end-to-end including network and client rendering?
01:45 Speaker 5 (Liam): Good call. We typically measure p95 as server-side generation latency (model forward pass + runtime overhead). End-to-end you'd add network RTT and client rendering. For benchmarks we'll provide both server-side numbers and suggested client-side offsets.
02:00 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Streaming — we need token/sec throughput to be consistent. We want at least ~20-40 tokens/sec per streaming session once generation starts. If you have batching across sessions, how does that affect streaming?
02:15 Speaker 5 (Liam): Continuous batching can improve throughput but introduces tradeoffs for tail latency. For strict p95 streaming you might reduce batching window or use per-request routing to low-batch lanes. Our Dedicated offering allows policy-based routing: latency-critical requests go to low-batch nodes, throughput-heavy bulk requests go to high-batch nodes.
02:36 Speaker 4 (Priya): From security side, we need to know data retention, encryption at rest, KMS integration for model keys, and SSO options. If we go Private, we need air-gapped options.
02:48 Speaker 1 (Sofia): We'll attach our security pack (SOC2 cert, KMS guide, SAML SSO walkthrough) after the call.
02:55 Speaker 3 (Mark): Benchmarking — what's the plan? We want to run our prompt set and a 24h traffic slice. Also interested in token/sec per GPU and tokens/sec per host at our concurrency patterns.
03:07 Speaker 5 (Liam): We usually do staged benchmarking: 1) small synthetic load to validate baselines (p95, median) 2) customer prompt set single-session profiling (to see token/sec and seq-length distribution) 3) scale up concurrency to your peak and run multi-session throughput tests with streaming enabled. We'll send a harness (JMeter style + a small client) you can run in your environment or we can run from Redwood on a test tenant.
03:32 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Can you share expected tokens/sec numbers for different models / quantization? e.g., 7B q4 vs 13B q4 and float 16?
03:40 Speaker 5 (Liam): Ballpark: on H100 with q4-type optimizations, optimized 7B variants can do ~400-800 tokens/sec single-session decode; 13B often 150-350 tokens/sec; 70B much lower, depends heavily on KV cache and cross-attention patterns. Those are very rough — we'll provide the bench matrix.
03:58 Speaker 3 (Mark): And per-GPU concurrency? If we have 50 concurrent sessions, what's per-GPU token/sec aggregate?
04:04 Speaker 5 (Liam): Depends on batching. With aggressive batching, a single H100 host serving many small sessions can approach thousands of tokens/sec aggregated, but per-session p95 may worsen. For latency critical lane we recommend fewer sessions per GPU or dedicated lane with CPU pinning and lower batch windows. We'll provide recommended concurrency density (e.g., 8-16 latency-critical sessions per GPU) vs throughput-optimized (50-200 sessions per GPU).
04:32 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Our UX requires first content within 100-200ms ideally; is that possible with Redwood?
04:39 Speaker 5 (Liam): For first token, yes in many cases we can get first token under 200ms on Dedicated with lightweight models and reserved capacity. But for models that do lots of compute or long contexts, first-token can be higher. Also network RTT matters. For streaming it's often more important to have consistent token/sec after first token.
04:58 Speaker 1 (Sofia): Quick question on fallbacks — if Dedicated is saturated, do you have automatic fallback to hosted or smaller models?
05:05 Speaker 5 (Liam): Yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants or different capacity tiers based on policy. You can set cost/latency preference per route. For production SLOs we often suggest a canary set-up: primary Dedicated pool plus fallback to hosted lower-cost pool for non-critical paths.
05:22 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Any constraints around streaming and function calls? We need the assistant to call internal APIs (sanitized) and then stream results back.
05:30 Speaker 5 (Liam): Function/tool calling with structured output is supported; streaming those outputs is supported too. The sequence is usually model generates structured JSON, we stream as tokens. For strict transactionality you can require the model to return final confirmed structure before committing, but UX-wise streaming partial fields is common.
05:48 Speaker 4 (Priya): Encryption — do you support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated?
05:53 Speaker 1 (Sofia): Yes, Dedicated supports KMS integration; Private supports BYOK and on-prem HSM options. We'll include docs.
06:02 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Cost — if we target p95 300ms and concurrency 50, roughly what cost band should we expect for Dedicated vs Hosted?
06:10 Speaker 5 (Liam): We'll produce an estimate in the pricing sheet. Very roughly Dedicated reserved capacity amortized can be cheaper per token at high sustained volume but requires a commitment. Hosted is easier to start and you pay per token; for spikes Dedicated plus burst-to-hosted can be the sweet spot. We'll put numbers for the workload you describe.
06:27 Speaker 3 (Mark): For benchmarks, we'll need metrics exposed: per-request p95, GPU utilization, batching windows, tokens/sec, and KV cache hit rate. Can Redwood surface those?
06:36 Speaker 5 (Liam): Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route latency breakdown, token-level cost, GPU metrics, trace IDs. We can add custom traces for your test runs too.
06:47 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Ok good. One more — data residency: Some of our data must remain in EU region.
06:52 Speaker 1 (Sofia): That's fine; we can pin regions and Dedicated/private can run in specific cloud regions. We'll note this for the pilot.
07:00 Speaker 3 (Mark): For the pilot, do you provision Dedicated nodes quickly? What's lead time?
07:05 Speaker 5 (Liam): Typical Dedicated provisioning is days to a week depending on capacity and region. We can prioritize if you have committed timeline.
07:12 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Timeline — we're aiming for pilot in late March and production by late April if benchmarks look good.
07:18 Speaker 1 (Sofia): Sounds reasonable. We'll aim to have pricing, bench plan and security pack to you by Wednesday.
07:25 Speaker 4 (Priya): Thanks. We'll review SOC2 report and follow up with questions.
07:29 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Quick clarifying Q: when you say p95 server-side, will you give the p95 for both non-streaming and streaming modes?
07:35 Speaker 5 (Liam): Yes. For streaming we typically report time-to-first-token p95 plus steady-state tokens/sec distribution p50/p95. For non-streaming generation we report full-completion p95.
07:47 Speaker 3 (Mark): Anything else on tooling integration? We use Prometheus and want to pull metrics.
07:52 Speaker 5 (Liam): Redwood supports metrics sinks (Prometheus, Datadog). We'll share exporter details.
07:59 Speaker 1 (Sofia): Ok wrapping up — recap of next steps, action items.
08:06 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.

End transcript.

Notes: Transcription may include minor mis-hearings (e.g., model names, instance types). References to GPUs (H100/A100) are approximate. Links mentioned: "security pack" (link to security docs), "benchmark harness" (repo link) — will be attached in follow-up email.
